narrowband.label: original (not compressed)
narrowband.note: The recording the others are compared against. 8 kHz, the same band today's codec is limited to.

narrowband.label: today: Spirit IPMR 6.4 kbit/s
narrowband.note: The 2007 codec, packetised exactly as the 3.3.5a client does: one 100 ms frame per datagram.

narrowband.label: Opus 6 kbit/s, 20 ms
narrowband.note: Opus narrowband at the same bitrate as today, in small packets.

narrowband.label: Opus 9.6 kbit/s, 100 ms packets
narrowband.note: Opus narrowband in the same packet shape as today. Largest packet is 117 bytes, inside the client's 124-byte cap.

narrowband.label: Opus 9.6 kbit/s, 60 ms packets
narrowband.note: The best measured balance: 13.1 kbit/s on the wire for a PESQ of 4.16.

narrowband.label: Opus 9.6 kbit/s, 20 ms packets
narrowband.note: Same audio in small packets. Best loss behaviour, but the per-packet overhead doubles the wire cost.

narrowband.label: Opus 12 kbit/s, 20 ms
narrowband.note: Narrowband ceiling: needs 150 bytes per 100 ms, so it no longer fits today's frame limit.

narrowband.label: Opus 15 kbit/s, 20 ms
narrowband.note: Above what narrowband can use. Included to show where narrowband stops improving.

narrowband.label: today: IPMR, 5 % loss
narrowband.note: What today's protocol does at 5 % packet loss: no concealment, the gaps are silence.

narrowband.label: Opus 9.6 kbit/s, 60 ms, 5 % loss + FEC
narrowband.note: Same 5 % loss with in-band forward error correction, which today's client has no equivalent of.

narrowband.label: Opus 9.6 kbit/s, 20 ms, 5 % loss + FEC
narrowband.note: Small packets shrink each loss to 20 ms, so the same loss pattern hurts less.

corpus: Open Speech Repository, American English, 8 kHz (voiptroubleshooter.com)
